2 Samuel 1.summary: Three days after David returns to Ziklag, a man of the Amalekites comes from Saul's camp with his clothes rent and earth on his head and says Saul and Jonathan are dead (2 Samuel 1:1–4). He claims that Saul leaned on his spear and asked him to slay him, so he did, and he brings Saul's crown and bracelet to David (2 Samuel 1:5–10). David and his men rend their clothes, mourn, weep, and fast until evening (2 Samuel 1:11–12). David asks How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed, and has the man put to death (2 Samuel 1:13–16). David sings a lament for Saul and Jonathan, the song of the bow, saying How are the mighty fallen, and tells Judah to learn it (2 Samuel 1:17–27).
2 Samuel 1.whereWeAre: 2 Samuel follows 1 Samuel, which ended with Saul's death on mount Gilboa. This chapter opens with David at Ziklag hearing the news from an Amalekite, and ends with David's song of grief for Saul and Jonathan (1:1-27). Chapter 2 tells how David becomes king over Judah.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Hears of Saul's death, mourns, has the messenger put to death, and sings the lament (1:11-27).

keyFigures.name: The Amalekite
keyFigures.role: Says he killed Saul, brings the crown and bracelet, and is put to death (1:2-16).

keyFigures.name: Saul
keyFigures.role: The dead king whose crown is brought to David (1:10,19-25).

keyFigures.name: Jonathan
keyFigures.role: Saul's son and David's friend, mourned in the song (1:25-26).

keyFigures.name: The people of Judah
keyFigures.role: Told to learn the song of the bow (1:18).

keyThemes.explanation: David weeps and fasts for Saul and Jonathan when he could have celebrated (1:11-12,17-27).
David puts the messenger to death for saying he killed the LORD's anointed (1:14-16).
David says Jonathan's love to him was wonderful (1:25-27).

2 Samuel 2.summary: David asks the LORD, and goes up to Hebron, where the men of Judah anoint him king over the house of Judah (2 Samuel 2:1–4). He sends word to the men of Jabeshgilead, blessing them for burying Saul (2 Samuel 2:4–7). Abner takes Ishbosheth, Saul's son, to Mahanaim and makes him king over Israel, and David reigns seven years and six months in Hebron (2 Samuel 2:8–11). Twelve men of each side meet at the pool of Gibeon and fall together, and a sore battle follows in which Abner's men are beaten (2 Samuel 2:12–17). Asahel, as light of foot as a wild roe, pursues Abner, and Abner smites him with the hinder end of the spear so that he dies (2 Samuel 2:18–23). Joab and Abishai pursue Abner until sunset, Abner cries Shall the sword devour for ever, and Joab blows the trumpet and stops the pursuit (2 Samuel 2:24–32).
2 Samuel 2.whereWeAre: Chapter 1 ended with David's lament. Chapter 2 shows David made king over Judah at Hebron while Abner makes Saul's son Ishbosheth king over the rest of Israel, and the two sides begin to fight at Gibeon (2:1-32). Chapter 3 tells how the war goes on.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Asks the LORD, goes to Hebron, and is anointed king over Judah (2:1-4).

keyFigures.name: Abner
keyFigures.role: Saul's captain, who makes Ishbosheth king and kills Asahel (2:8-9,23).

keyFigures.name: Ishbosheth
keyFigures.role: Saul's son, made king over Israel at Mahanaim (2:8-10).

keyFigures.name: Joab and Abishai
keyFigures.role: David's men, who pursue Abner after Asahel's death (2:18,24).

keyFigures.name: Asahel
keyFigures.role: Joab's brother, light of foot as a wild roe, slain by Abner (2:18-23).

keyFigures.name: The men of Jabeshgilead
keyFigures.role: Blessed by David for burying Saul (2:4-7).

keyThemes.explanation: David asks the LORD whether to go up and where (2:1).
Judah follows David while Abner sets up Ishbosheth over Israel (2:4,8-10).
Men of Israel fight men of Israel, and Asahel dies (2:12-32).

2 Samuel 3.summary: There is long war between the house of Saul and the house of David, but David waxes stronger and stronger, and six sons are born to him at Hebron (2 Samuel 3:1–5). Ishbosheth accuses Abner about Saul's concubine Rizpah, and Abner is very wroth and promises to bring all Israel to David (2 Samuel 3:6–12). David asks for his wife Michal back, Abner talks to the elders of Israel, and he comes to David at Hebron and is sent away in peace (2 Samuel 3:13–21). Joab hears of it, calls Abner back, takes him aside in the gate, and smites him under the fifth rib for the blood of Asahel (2 Samuel 3:22–27). David says he and his kingdom are guiltless before the LORD, curses Joab's house, and mourns Abner with all the people, saying Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel (2 Samuel 3:28–39).
2 Samuel 3.whereWeAre: Chapter 2 ended with the first fight between the two sides. Chapter 3 tells how Abner turns to David after a quarrel with Ishbosheth, and how Joab kills him, and how David mourns him (3:1-39). Chapter 4 tells how Ishbosheth himself is killed.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Grows stronger, makes peace with Abner, and openly mourns him (3:1,17-21,31-39).

keyFigures.name: Abner
keyFigures.role: Quarrels with Ishbosheth, offers Israel to David, and is killed by Joab (3:6-12,27).

keyFigures.name: Ishbosheth
keyFigures.role: Accuses Abner and loses his backing (3:7-11).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Kills Abner to avenge his brother Asahel (3:26-27,30).

keyFigures.name: Michal
keyFigures.role: Saul's daughter, taken from her husband and brought back to David (3:13-16).

keyThemes.explanation: Abner promises to bring all Israel over to David (3:6-21).
Joab kills Abner in the gate for the blood of his brother (3:26-30).
David curses the deed, fasts, and walks behind the bier (3:28-39).

2 Samuel 4.summary: When Saul's son Ishbosheth hears that Abner is dead, his hands are feeble and all Israel is troubled (2 Samuel 4:1). The chapter mentions Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, who is lame on his feet because he fell when his nurse fled (2 Samuel 4:4). Baanah and Rechab, captains of bands, go in at the heat of the day while Ishbosheth lies on his bed at noon, smite him, and take his head to David at Hebron (2 Samuel 4:2–8). David says As the LORD liveth, he slew the man who brought him news of Saul, and how much more when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed (2 Samuel 4:9–11). David commands his young men to slay them, and they cut off their hands and feet and hang them up over the pool in Hebron (2 Samuel 4:12).
2 Samuel 4.whereWeAre: Chapter 3 ended with David mourning Abner. Chapter 4 tells how two captains murder Ishbosheth in his bed to win a reward, and how David has them put to death (4:1-12). Chapter 5 tells how all Israel makes David king.

keyFigures.name: Ishbosheth
keyFigures.role: Saul's son, whose hands become feeble, killed on his bed at noon (4:1,5-7).

keyFigures.name: Baanah and Rechab
keyFigures.role: Captains of bands who kill Ishbosheth and bring his head to David (4:2,5-8).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Says wicked men have slain a righteous person, and has them put to death (4:9-12).

keyFigures.name: Mephibosheth
keyFigures.role: Jonathan's son, lame on his feet from childhood (4:4).

keyThemes.theme: A king who has lost heart
keyThemes.explanation: Ishbosheth is feeble after Abner dies (4:1).
Baanah and Rechab expect thanks and receive death (4:8-12).
Mephibosheth became lame when his nurse fled with him at the news of Saul's death (4:4).

2 Samuel 5.summary: All the tribes of Israel come to David at Hebron and say Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh, and they anoint him king over Israel, and he is thirty years old and reigns forty years (2 Samuel 5:1–5). David and his men take the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites, who had said the blind and the lame would keep him out, and he dwells in the fort and calls it the city of David (2 Samuel 5:6–10). Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to build David a house, and David perceives that the LORD has established him king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:11–12). More sons and daughters are born to David in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:13–16). The Philistines come up against David twice in the valley of Rephaim, and each time David enquires of the LORD, who gives him victory, the second time when he hears the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees (2 Samuel 5:17–25).
2 Samuel 5.whereWeAre: Chapter 4 ended with the murder of Ishbosheth. Chapter 5 shows all Israel anointing David at Hebron, David taking Jerusalem and making it his city, and David twice beating the Philistines after asking the LORD (5:1-25). Chapter 6 brings the ark to Jerusalem.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Anointed over all Israel, takes Zion, and beats the Philistines after asking the LORD (5:3-10,17-25).

keyFigures.name: The elders of Israel
keyFigures.role: Come to Hebron and anoint David king (5:1-3).

keyFigures.name: The Jebusites
keyFigures.role: Say the blind and the lame can keep David out of Zion (5:6).

keyFigures.name: Hiram king of Tyre
keyFigures.role: Sends cedar trees, carpenters, and masons (5:11).

keyFigures.name: The Philistines
keyFigures.role: Come up twice against David in the valley of Rephaim (5:17-25).

keyFigures.name: The LORD
keyFigures.role: Goes before David and gives him victory (5:10,19,24).

keyThemes.explanation: The tribes say they are David's bone and flesh, and the LORD said he would feed his people (5:1-5).
David takes Zion and makes Jerusalem his capital (5:6-12).
David enquires of the LORD both times before facing the Philistines (5:19,23-25).

explainedReferences.explanation: Same event: Israel's elders anointing David as king at Hebron.
Same event: David's capture of Jerusalem from the Jebusites.

2 Samuel 6.summary: David gathers thirty thousand chosen men and sets the ark of God on a new cart to bring it from Baale of Judah, and Uzzah and Ahio drive it while David and all Israel play before the LORD (2 Samuel 6:1–5). When the oxen shake the ark, Uzzah puts forth his hand and takes hold of it, and God smites him there for his error and he dies (2 Samuel 6:6–7). David is displeased and afraid, and says How shall the ark of the LORD come to me, and he leaves it in the house of Obededom the Gittite, whom the LORD blesses for three months (2 Samuel 6:8–11). David brings up the ark with gladness, offers an ox and a fatling after six paces, and dances before the LORD with all his might, girded with a linen ephod (2 Samuel 6:12–15). He sets the ark in a tent, offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, and gives every man a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine (2 Samuel 6:16–19). Michal despises David for dancing, and he answers that it was before the LORD, and she has no child to the day of her death (2 Samuel 6:20–23).
2 Samuel 6.whereWeAre: Chapter 5 ended with David's victories over the Philistines. Chapter 6 tells how David brings the ark to Jerusalem, stops after Uzzah dies, and then brings it in with joy, which Michal despises (6:1-23). Chapter 7 gives the LORD's promise to David.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Brings the ark to Jerusalem, is afraid after Uzzah dies, and dances before the LORD (6:1-5,9,14-15).

keyFigures.name: Uzzah
keyFigures.role: Takes hold of the ark when the oxen shake it and dies (6:6-7).

keyFigures.name: Obededom the Gittite
keyFigures.role: Keeps the ark in his house three months and is blessed (6:10-12).

keyFigures.name: The thirty thousand men of Israel
keyFigures.role: Go with David to bring up the ark (6:1-5,15).

keyFigures.name: Michal
keyFigures.role: Looks through a window, despises David, and has no child (6:16,20-23).

keyThemes.explanation: Uzzah dies for putting his hand on the ark, and David fears to move it (6:6-11).
David dances with all his might and shares food with the people (6:12-19).
Michal thinks David has shamed himself, and he says he will be yet more vile than thus (6:20-23).

explainedReferences.explanation: Same event: Bringing the ark to Jerusalem and Michal seeing David dance.

2 Samuel 7.summary: David sits in his house of cedar, and the LORD has given him rest, and he tells Nathan the prophet that the ark of God dwells within curtains, and Nathan tells him to do all that is in his heart (2 Samuel 7:1–3). That night the word of the LORD comes to Nathan, who is to ask David Shalt thou build me an house, since the LORD never asked for one in all his walking with Israel (2 Samuel 7:4–7). The LORD says he took David from the sheepcote to be ruler over his people, made him a great name, and will give Israel a place (2 Samuel 7:8–11). The LORD will make David an house, and set up his seed after him, who shall build an house for his name, and he will be his father, and he shall be his son, and David's house and kingdom shall be established for ever (2 Samuel 7:11–16). Nathan tells David all this, and David sits before the LORD and says Who am I, O Lord GOD, and asks him to do as he has said, that his name be magnified for ever (2 Samuel 7:17–29).
2 Samuel 7.whereWeAre: Chapter 6 ended with the ark in Jerusalem. Chapter 7 shows David wanting to build God a house, and the LORD saying he will build David a house instead, a family line that will last for ever, which is the great promise of this book (7:1-29). Chapter 8 tells of David's victories.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Wants to build a house for the ark, then sits before the LORD in thanks (7:1-3,18-29).

keyFigures.name: Nathan
keyFigures.role: Tells David to go ahead, then brings the LORD's word that night (7:3-17).

keyFigures.name: The LORD
keyFigures.role: Promises David a house, a son, and a throne for ever (7:8-16).

keyFigures.name: David's seed
keyFigures.role: The son who will build an house for the LORD's name (7:12-13).

keyThemes.explanation: David wants to build a house for the LORD, and the LORD says he will build David's house (7:1-11).
The LORD says David's house and kingdom shall be established for ever (7:12-16).
David asks Who am I, O Lord GOD, and praises him (7:18-29).

explainedReferences.explanation: Same event: God's covenant promise to David through Nathan.
Promise to be a father to David's descendant.

2 Samuel 8.summary: David smites the Philistines and takes Methegammah, and he smites Moab, measures them with a line, and makes them servants who bring gifts (2 Samuel 8:1–2). He smites Hadadezer king of Zobah, and when the Syrians of Damascus help him, David slays twenty and two thousand of them and puts garrisons in Syria (2 Samuel 8:3–8). Toi king of Hamath sends his son Joram with vessels of silver, gold, and brass, and David dedicates them to the LORD with the other silver and gold from the nations he subdued (2 Samuel 8:9–12). David gets him a name when he smites eighteen thousand Edomites in the valley of salt, and the LORD preserves David whithersoever he goes (2 Samuel 8:13–14). David reigns over all Israel and executes judgment and justice, and the chapter lists his officers, Joab, Jehoshaphat, Zadok, Ahimelech, Seraiah, and Benaiah (2 Samuel 8:15–18).
2 Samuel 8.whereWeAre: Chapter 7 gave the promise of a lasting house. Chapter 8 lists David's wars against the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Syria, and Edom, and the officers who help him rule (8:1-18). Chapter 9 shows his kindness to Jonathan's son.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Wins his wars, dedicates the silver and gold to the LORD, and executes judgment and justice (8:1-15).

keyFigures.name: Hadadezer king of Zobah
keyFigures.role: Smitten by David as he went to recover his border at the river (8:3-8).

keyFigures.name: Toi king of Hamath
keyFigures.role: Sends his son Joram with gifts when Hadadezer falls (8:9-10).

keyFigures.name: The LORD
keyFigures.role: Preserves David whithersoever he goes (8:6,14).

keyFigures.name: David's officers
keyFigures.role: Joab, Jehoshaphat, Zadok, Ahimelech, Seraiah, and Benaiah (8:16-18).

keyThemes.explanation: The text says twice that the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went (8:6,14).
David reigns over all Israel and executes judgment and justice unto all his people (8:15).
David dedicates the silver and gold from the nations to the LORD (8:11-12).

2 Samuel 9.summary: David asks Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan's sake (2 Samuel 9:1). Ziba, a servant of Saul's house, tells him of a son of Jonathan who is lame on his feet, living in Lodebar in the house of Machir (2 Samuel 9:2–5). Mephibosheth comes and falls on his face, and David says Fear not, for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore all the land of Saul to him (2 Samuel 9:6–8). Mephibosheth is to eat bread at David's table continually, and Ziba and his fifteen sons and twenty servants are to farm his land, and Mephibosheth eats at the king's table as one of the king's sons (2 Samuel 9:9–13).
2 Samuel 9.whereWeAre: Chapter 8 listed David's wars and officers. Chapter 9 turns to one quiet act: David keeps his promise to Jonathan by bringing Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth to eat at the king's table (9:1-13). Chapter 10 returns to war, with Ammon.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Asks after Saul's house and shews kindness for Jonathan's sake (9:1,7-11).

keyFigures.name: Mephibosheth
keyFigures.role: Jonathan's lame son, restored to Saul's land and seated at the king's table (9:6-13).

keyFigures.name: Ziba
keyFigures.role: Saul's servant, who tells David about Mephibosheth and is told to farm his land (9:2-3,9-12).

keyFigures.name: Machir son of Ammiel
keyFigures.role: Keeps Mephibosheth in Lodebar (9:4-5).

keyThemes.explanation: David acts for Jonathan's sake, as he had sworn (9:1,7).
Mephibosheth eats at the king's table continually, as one of the king's sons (9:7-13).
David gives back Saul's land and tells Ziba to farm it (9:9-11).

2 Samuel 10.summary: When Nahash king of the Ammonites dies, David sends servants to comfort his son Hanun, but the princes of Ammon say David has sent spies, and Hanun shaves off half the beard of each servant and cuts their garments to the buttocks (2 Samuel 10:1–5). David tells his men to tarry at Jericho until their beards are grown (2 Samuel 10:5). The Ammonites hire twenty thousand Syrians of Bethrehob and Zoba, a thousand of the king of Maacah, and twelve thousand men of Ishtob, and Joab sets the battle in array against both (2 Samuel 10:6–9). Joab says Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and the LORD do that which seemeth him good, and the Syrians and the Ammonites flee (2 Samuel 10:10–14). Hadarezer brings in Syrians from beyond the river, and David passes over Jordan to Helam and slays seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen, and the kings who served Hadarezer make peace with Israel and fear to help Ammon any more (2 Samuel 10:15–19).
2 Samuel 10.whereWeAre: Chapter 9 ended with Mephibosheth at David's table. Chapter 10 tells how David's kind message to Ammon is insulted, which leads to war with Ammon and Syria (10:1-19). Chapter 11 begins with the siege of Rabbah and David's great sin.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Sends comfort to Hanun and then fights Ammon and the Syrians (10:2,17-18).

keyFigures.name: Hanun
keyFigures.role: King of Ammon, who shames David's servants (10:1-4).

keyFigures.name: The princes of the Ammonites
keyFigures.role: Tell Hanun that David's servants are spies (10:3).

keyFigures.name: Joab and Abishai
keyFigures.role: Divide the army and fight the Syrians and Ammonites (10:9-14).

keyFigures.name: The Syrians
keyFigures.role: Hired by Ammon, then beaten and made peace with Israel (10:6,13-19).

keyThemes.explanation: Hanun's princes say David's comforters are spies (10:1-4).
Joab says Be of good courage and the LORD do that which seemeth him good (10:11-12).
The fight with Ammon grows into a war with Syria (10:6-19).

explainedReferences.explanation: Same event: The conflict involving David's messengers, Ammon, and Aram.

2 Samuel 11.summary: At the time when kings go forth to battle, David sends Joab and the army against Ammon to besiege Rabbah, but David tarries still at Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1). One evening David walks on the roof of the king's house and sees a woman washing, very beautiful, and learns she is Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11:2–3). David sends messengers and takes her, and lies with her, and she sends word I am with child (2 Samuel 11:4–5). David sends for Uriah and tells him to go down to his house, but Uriah sleeps at the door of the king's house, saying The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents (2 Samuel 11:6–13). David makes Uriah drunk, but he still does not go home, so David writes a letter to Joab, sent by Uriah's own hand, to set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle and retire from him (2 Samuel 11:14–17). Uriah is slain, David tells the messenger Let not this thing displease thee, and when Bathsheba's mourning is past, David brings her to his house, and she bears a son, but the thing that David had done displeased the LORD (2 Samuel 11:18–27).
2 Samuel 11.whereWeAre: Chapter 10 ended with Ammon's allies afraid to help again. Chapter 11 tells how, while the army besieges Rabbah, David takes Bathsheba and has her husband Uriah killed in battle, and the LORD is displeased (11:1-27). Chapter 12 tells how Nathan confronts him.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Stays in Jerusalem, takes Bathsheba, and arranges for Uriah to be killed (11:1-4,14-15,27).

keyFigures.name: Bathsheba
keyFigures.role: The wife of Uriah, who is taken by David and bears his son (11:3-5,26-27).

keyFigures.name: Uriah the Hittite
keyFigures.role: A loyal soldier who will not go home while the ark and the army are in tents, and is killed (11:6-17).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Carries out David's letter at the siege of Rabbah (11:1,14-25).

keyFigures.name: The messenger
keyFigures.role: Brings David word of the battle and of Uriah's death (11:18-24).

keyThemes.explanation: The king sends for a woman and then for her husband's death (11:2-5,14-17).
David tries to bring Uriah home so the child will seem his, and when that fails, has him killed (11:6-17).
The chapter ends by saying the thing that David had done displeased the LORD (11:26-27).

2 Samuel 12.summary: The LORD sends Nathan to David, who tells of a rich man who took a poor man's one little ewe lamb for his guest, and David says the man shall surely die and restore the lamb fourfold (2 Samuel 12:1–6). Nathan says Thou art the man, tells David what the LORD gave him, and says because he despised the commandment and killed Uriah, the sword shall never depart from his house (2 Samuel 12:7–12). David says I have sinned against the LORD, and Nathan says The LORD also hath put away thy sin, thou shalt not die, but the child shall surely die (2 Samuel 12:13–14). David fasts and lies all night on the earth while the child is sick, and when the child dies on the seventh day, he rises, washes, worships in the house of the LORD, and eats, saying I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me (2 Samuel 12:15–23). David comforts Bathsheba, and she bears Solomon, and the LORD loves him, and Nathan calls his name Jedidiah (2 Samuel 12:24–25). Joab fights Rabbah and sends for David to take the city, and David takes the crown of their king and brings out the spoil (2 Samuel 12:26–31).
2 Samuel 12.whereWeAre: Chapter 11 ended with the LORD displeased at David. Chapter 12 shows Nathan telling a story that makes David judge himself, David confessing, the first child dying, and Solomon born, while Rabbah falls (12:1-31). Chapter 13 shows the trouble in David's house.

keyFigures.name: Nathan
keyFigures.role: Tells the story of the poor man's lamb and says Thou art the man (12:1-12).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Says I have sinned, fasts for the child, and then takes Rabbah (12:5-7,13,16-23,29-31).

keyFigures.name: Bathsheba
keyFigures.role: Loses her first child and later bears Solomon (12:15-24).

keyFigures.name: Solomon
keyFigures.role: Born to David and Bathsheba, loved by the LORD, and called Jedidiah (12:24-25).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Fights Rabbah and calls David to take the city (12:26-28).

keyThemes.theme: A story that shows the sin
keyThemes.explanation: Nathan's tale of the lamb makes David judge the man, then hear Thou art the man (12:1-7).
The LORD puts away his sin, yet the sword will not leave his house and the child dies (12:10-23).
Solomon is born, and the LORD loves him (12:24-25).

2 Samuel 13.summary: Absalom has a fair sister, Tamar, and his half brother Amnon loves her, and Jonadab, a very subtil man, tells Amnon to lie down and make himself sick (2 Samuel 13:1–5). David sends Tamar to make cakes for him, and Amnon sends the others out, and she says Nay, my brother, do not force me, for no such thing ought to be done in Israel, but he forces her and then hates her exceedingly and has her put out (2 Samuel 13:6–18). Tamar puts ashes on her head, rends her garment, and goes crying, and Absalom takes her in, and she remains desolate in his house, and David is very wroth but does nothing (2 Samuel 13:19–22). After two full years Absalom invites the king's sons to sheepshearing at Baalhazor and has his servants kill Amnon when his heart is merry with wine (2 Samuel 13:23–29). David hears a false report that all the sons are dead, and Jonadab says only Amnon is dead, and Absalom flees to Talmai king of Geshur and stays three years, and David mourns and longs to go to Absalom (2 Samuel 13:30–39).
2 Samuel 13.whereWeAre: Chapter 12 ended with Rabbah taken. Chapter 13 shows the sword in David's house, as Nathan said: Amnon wrongs his half sister Tamar, and her brother Absalom has Amnon killed and runs away (13:1-39). Chapter 14 tells how Absalom comes back.

keyFigures.name: Tamar
keyFigures.role: David's daughter, who tells Amnon Nay, my brother, do not force me, and is wronged and left desolate (13:1,11-20).

keyFigures.name: Amnon
keyFigures.role: David's son, who wrongs Tamar and then hates her, and is killed (13:1-17,28-29).

keyFigures.name: Absalom
keyFigures.role: Tamar's brother, who waits two years and then has Amnon killed (13:20-29).

keyFigures.name: Jonadab
keyFigures.role: Amnon's friend, a very subtil man, who plans the trick (13:3-5,32-35).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Is very wroth but does nothing, and later mourns (13:21,31,37-39).

keyFigures.name: Talmai king of Geshur
keyFigures.role: Absalom's mother's father, to whom Absalom flees (13:37-38).

keyThemes.explanation: Tamar pleads with Amnon, but he forces her and puts her out (13:10-18).
David is very wroth but does not act, and Absalom hates Amnon (13:21-22).
Absalom has Amnon killed at the sheepshearing and flees (13:23-39).

2 Samuel 14.summary: Joab sees that the king's heart is toward Absalom and sends to Tekoa for a wise woman and tells her to feign herself a mourner (2 Samuel 14:1–3). She tells David a story of two sons, one of whom has killed the other, and her family wants to put the survivor to death and quench her coal that is left, and David says not one hair of her son shall fall to the earth (2 Samuel 14:4–11). She says the king is as one which is faulty in not fetching home his banished, for we must needs die, as water spilt on the ground, but God devises means that his banished be not expelled from him (2 Samuel 14:12–17). David asks Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this, and tells Joab to bring Absalom home but not to see his face (2 Samuel 14:18–24). Absalom, whose hair weighs two hundred shekels and who has three sons and a daughter Tamar, lives two full years in Jerusalem without seeing the king (2 Samuel 14:25–28). Absalom has Joab's field of barley set on fire to make him come, and then says let me see the king's face, and the king kisses him (2 Samuel 14:29–33).
2 Samuel 14.whereWeAre: Chapter 13 ended with Absalom in Geshur. Chapter 14 tells how Joab uses a wise woman of Tekoa to move David to bring Absalom home, though David will not see him for two years until Absalom sets Joab's field on fire (14:1-33). Chapter 15 tells how Absalom turns on his father.

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Sends the woman of Tekoa to plead for Absalom and later brings him to the king (14:1-3,21-24,29-33).

keyFigures.name: The wise woman of Tekoa
keyFigures.role: Tells David a made-up story of two sons (14:2-20).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Lets Absalom come home but will not see him for two years, then kisses him (14:21-24,33).

keyFigures.name: Absalom
keyFigures.role: Comes home, has Joab's field burned, and says let me see the king's face (14:24-33).

keyThemes.theme: A story to move the king
keyThemes.explanation: The woman of Tekoa tells David a tale that shows him what he is doing to Absalom (14:4-17).
Absalom lives in Jerusalem two years without seeing his father's face (14:24,28).
He burns Joab's barley field to get Joab to come (14:29-32).

2 Samuel 15.summary: Absalom prepares chariots, horses, and fifty men to run before him, and he rises early and stands by the way of the gate, telling all who come with a matter for the king that there is no man deputed to hear them, and he steals the hearts of the men of Israel (2 Samuel 15:1–6). After forty years, as the KJV has it, Absalom asks leave to pay a vow in Hebron, and sends spies through Israel to say Absalom reigneth in Hebron, and Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, joins him (2 Samuel 15:7–12). David says Arise, and let us flee, and leaves ten concubines to keep the house (2 Samuel 15:13–16). Ittai the Gittite says As the LORD liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, there also will thy servant be (2 Samuel 15:17–22). Zadok and the Levites bring the ark, but David says Carry back the ark of God into the city, and if the LORD has no delight in him, let him do as seemeth good unto him (2 Samuel 15:23–29). David goes up the mount of Olives weeping, with his head covered and barefoot, and prays that the LORD turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness (2 Samuel 15:30–31). He sends Hushai back to Absalom to defeat Ahithophel's counsel (2 Samuel 15:32–37).
2 Samuel 15.whereWeAre: Chapter 14 ended with the king kissing Absalom. Chapter 15 tells how Absalom wins the hearts of Israel, sets up as king at Hebron, and how David leaves Jerusalem weeping, sends the ark back, and sends Hushai to work against Ahithophel (15:1-37). Chapter 16 follows David in flight.

keyFigures.name: Absalom
keyFigures.role: Wins the people at the gate and makes himself king at Hebron (15:1-12).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Flees Jerusalem, sends back the ark, and prays against Ahithophel (15:13-16,25-31).

keyFigures.name: Ahithophel
keyFigures.role: David's counsellor, who joins Absalom (15:12,31).

keyFigures.name: Ittai the Gittite
keyFigures.role: A stranger who swears to follow David in death or life (15:19-22).

keyFigures.name: Zadok and Abiathar
keyFigures.role: The priests who bring the ark and then take it back (15:24-29).

keyFigures.name: Hushai the Archite
keyFigures.role: David's friend, sent back to defeat Ahithophel's counsel (15:32-37).

keyThemes.explanation: Absalom tells people the king has no one to hear them and says Oh that I were made judge (15:2-6).
Ittai the Gittite swears to follow David wherever he goes (15:19-22).
David sends the ark back and says let him do to me as seemeth good unto him (15:25-26).

2 Samuel 16.summary: Ziba meets David with two asses, bread, and fruit, and says Mephibosheth stays in Jerusalem hoping the house of Israel will restore him his father's kingdom, and David says all that belonged to Mephibosheth is Ziba's (2 Samuel 16:1–4). At Bahurim, Shimei the son of Gera curses David and throws stones, saying Come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial (2 Samuel 16:5–8). Abishai asks leave to take off his head, but David says let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David, and it may be that the LORD will look on his affliction (2 Samuel 16:9–14). Hushai comes to Absalom and says God save the king, and says he will serve the one whom the LORD and this people choose (2 Samuel 16:15–19). Ahithophel tells Absalom to go in unto his father's concubines, and Absalom does so in the sight of all Israel on a tent on the top of the house (2 Samuel 16:20–23).
2 Samuel 16.whereWeAre: Chapter 15 ended with Hushai going into Jerusalem. Chapter 16 shows David on the road meeting Ziba and Shimei, and Absalom taking Jerusalem and taking Ahithophel's counsel to claim his father's house (16:1-23). Chapter 17 tells whose advice Absalom takes next.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Gives Mephibosheth's land to Ziba and bears Shimei's cursing (16:1-4,9-13).

keyFigures.name: Ziba
keyFigures.role: Meets David with food and says his master hopes for the kingdom (16:1-4).

keyFigures.name: Shimei
keyFigures.role: A man of Saul's house who curses David and throws stones (16:5-8,13).

keyFigures.name: Abishai
keyFigures.role: Offers to take off Shimei's head (16:9).

keyFigures.name: Hushai
keyFigures.role: Joins Absalom's court as David asked (16:16-19).

keyFigures.name: Absalom and Ahithophel
keyFigures.role: Absalom takes Jerusalem and follows Ahithophel's counsel (16:15,20-23).

keyThemes.explanation: David gives away Mephibosheth's land after hearing only Ziba (16:1-4).
David tells Abishai let him curse, because the LORD hath bidden him (16:9-13).

keyThemes.theme: A public claim to the throne
keyThemes.explanation: Absalom goes in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel (16:20-23).

2 Samuel 17.summary: Ahithophel tells Absalom to let him take twelve thousand men and pursue David that night and smite the king only (2 Samuel 17:1–4). Hushai says that counsel is not good, for David and his men are chafed in their minds as a bear robbed of her whelps, and Absalom should gather all Israel and go to battle himself (2 Samuel 17:5–13). Absalom and Israel say the counsel of Hushai is better than the counsel of Ahithophel, for the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel (2 Samuel 17:14). Hushai tells Zadok and Abiathar, and Jonathan and Ahimaaz carry the word to David, hidden by a woman at Bahurim in a well, and David and all the people pass over Jordan before morning (2 Samuel 17:15–22). Ahithophel sees his counsel not followed, saddles his ass, puts his household in order, and hangs himself (2 Samuel 17:23). David comes to Mahanaim, and Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai bring beds, basins, wheat, barley, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese for the people, while Absalom passes over Jordan with Amasa (2 Samuel 17:24–29).
2 Samuel 17.whereWeAre: Chapter 16 ended with Absalom taking his father's house. Chapter 17 tells how Absalom takes Hushai's advice over Ahithophel's, how David gets word and crosses the Jordan, and how Ahithophel hangs himself (17:1-29). Chapter 18 tells of the battle.

keyFigures.name: Ahithophel
keyFigures.role: Advises a quick strike at David and hangs himself when it is refused (17:1-4,23).

keyFigures.name: Hushai
keyFigures.role: Persuades Absalom to wait and gather all Israel, and sends word to David (17:5-16).

keyFigures.name: Absalom
keyFigures.role: Takes Hushai's counsel and crosses the Jordan with Amasa (17:14,24-26).

keyFigures.name: Jonathan and Ahimaaz
keyFigures.role: Priests' sons who carry the warning to David (17:17-21).

keyFigures.name: The woman at Bahurim
keyFigures.role: Hides the two messengers in a well (17:18-20).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Crosses the Jordan and comes to Mahanaim, where friends feed his people (17:22,24,27-29).

keyThemes.explanation: Ahithophel's plan is quick and sharp, and Hushai's is slow and large (17:1-13).
The LORD appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel (17:14).
A woman at Bahurim hides the messengers in a well, and friends at Mahanaim bring food (17:17-20,27-29).

2 Samuel 18.summary: David numbers the people and divides them into three companies under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, and the people will not let him go out to battle, saying thou art worth ten thousand of us (2 Samuel 18:1–4). David charges the three captains in the hearing of all, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom (2 Samuel 18:5). The battle in the wood of Ephraim kills twenty thousand, and the wood devours more people that day than the sword (2 Samuel 18:6–8). Absalom's head is caught in the thick boughs of a great oak as he rides a mule, and a man tells Joab, who will not wait and thrusts three darts through the heart of Absalom, and ten young men smite him, and they cast him into a great pit in the wood (2 Samuel 18:9–18). Ahimaaz and the Cushite run with the news, and David asks Is the young man Absalom safe, and when he hears, he goes up to the chamber over the gate and weeps, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom, would God I had died for thee (2 Samuel 18:19–33).
2 Samuel 18.whereWeAre: Chapter 17 ended with David at Mahanaim. Chapter 18 tells how David's army beats Absalom's in the wood of Ephraim, how Joab kills Absalom against David's wish, and how David mourns (18:1-33). Chapter 19 tells how the victory turns to shame.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Tells his captains to deal gently with Absalom, then weeps for him (18:5,24-33).

keyFigures.name: Absalom
keyFigures.role: Caught by his head in an oak and killed by Joab (18:9-15).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Thrusts three darts through Absalom's heart against the king's charge (18:10-15).

keyFigures.name: Abishai and Ittai
keyFigures.role: The other two captains over the thirds (18:2,5).

keyFigures.name: The man who saw Absalom
keyFigures.role: Will not touch Absalom for a thousand shekels, because the king charged them (18:10-13).

keyFigures.name: Ahimaaz and the Cushite
keyFigures.role: Run with the tidings to David (18:19-32).

keyThemes.theme: A king who is also a father
keyThemes.explanation: David asks the captains to deal gently with Absalom (18:5).

keyThemes.theme: Joab does what he is told not to
keyThemes.explanation: Joab kills Absalom although David had told them to spare him (18:10-15).
David cries O my son Absalom, would God I had died for thee (18:33).

2 Samuel 19.summary: Joab is told that the king weeps and mourns for Absalom, so the victory that day is turned into mourning, and the people steal into the city as if they had fled in battle (2 Samuel 19:1–3). Joab tells David that he has shamed the faces of all his servants, loving his enemies and hating his friends, and says go forth and speak comfortably or no man will tarry with him this night (2 Samuel 19:4–7). The king sits in the gate, and David sends to the elders of Judah, saying ye are my bones and my flesh, and makes Amasa captain in Joab's room, and Judah comes to Gilgal to bring him over Jordan (2 Samuel 19:8–15). Shimei falls down and says Let not my lord impute iniquity, and David swears he shall not die, though Abishai would have had him put to death (2 Samuel 19:16–23). Mephibosheth, who has not dressed his feet nor trimmed his beard, says Ziba deceived him, and David says Thou and Ziba divide the land, and Mephibosheth says let him take all (2 Samuel 19:24–30). Barzillai, fourscore years old, brings the king over Jordan but will not go with him to Jerusalem, and Judah and Israel quarrel over the king, and the words of Judah are fiercer (2 Samuel 19:31–43).
2 Samuel 19.whereWeAre: Chapter 18 ended with David's cry for Absalom. Chapter 19 tells how Joab makes David face his men, how David returns across the Jordan, deals with Shimei, Mephibosheth, and Barzillai, and how Judah and Israel begin to quarrel (19:1-43). Chapter 20 tells how that quarrel breaks out.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Is rebuked by Joab, then crosses the Jordan and forgives Shimei (19:5-8,16-23).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Tells David he has shamed his servants and must speak comfortably to them (19:5-7).

keyFigures.name: Shimei
keyFigures.role: Falls down and begs David not to impute iniquity (19:18-20).

keyFigures.name: Mephibosheth
keyFigures.role: Says Ziba deceived him, and will let Ziba take all (19:24-30).

keyFigures.name: Barzillai
keyFigures.role: Fourscore years old, who will not go to court (19:31-39).

keyFigures.name: Amasa
keyFigures.role: Made captain of the host in Joab's room (19:13).

keyThemes.theme: A king must face his men
keyThemes.explanation: Joab says go forth and speak comfortably, or no man will stay with you (19:5-8).
David spares Shimei and hears Mephibosheth's side of the story (19:16-30).
Judah and Israel quarrel over who has more right in the king (19:40-43).

2 Samuel 20.summary: Sheba, a son of Bichri and a Benjamite, blows a trumpet and says We have no part in David, every man to his tents, O Israel, and all Israel follows him while Judah clings to the king (2 Samuel 20:1–2). David comes to Jerusalem and puts the ten concubines in ward, and they live in widowhood (2 Samuel 20:3). David tells Amasa to gather Judah in three days, but he tarries, so David tells Abishai to pursue Sheba, and Joab goes out with him (2 Samuel 20:4–7). At Gibeon Joab takes Amasa by the beard to kiss him and smites him in the fifth rib, and a man calls He that favoureth Joab, and he that is for David, let him go after Joab (2 Samuel 20:8–13). Joab besieges Sheba in Abel of Bethmaachah and casts up a bank against the city (2 Samuel 20:14–15). A wise woman calls from the wall, asking why Joab would swallow up the inheritance of the LORD, and her city throws Sheba's head over the wall, and Joab blows the trumpet and goes home (2 Samuel 20:16–22). The chapter lists David's officers (2 Samuel 20:23–26).
2 Samuel 20.whereWeAre: Chapter 19 ended with Judah and Israel quarrelling. Chapter 20 shows the quarrel become a revolt under Sheba, Joab murdering Amasa, and a wise woman saving her city by giving up Sheba (20:1-26). Chapter 21 begins the closing chapters of the book.

keyFigures.name: Sheba son of Bichri
keyFigures.role: A Benjamite who calls Israel to leave David (20:1-2,14,22).

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Puts the ten concubines in ward and sends Abishai after Sheba (20:3-7).

keyFigures.name: Amasa
keyFigures.role: Is slow to gather Judah and is killed by Joab (20:4-5,8-12).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Kills Amasa and besieges Abel of Bethmaachah (20:8-15,22).

keyFigures.name: The wise woman of Abel
keyFigures.role: Speaks from the wall and has Sheba's head thrown over (20:16-22).

keyThemes.explanation: Sheba calls every man to his tents, and most of Israel goes with him (20:1-2).
Joab takes Amasa by the beard and smites him with a hidden sword (20:8-13).

keyThemes.theme: A wise woman saves a city
keyThemes.explanation: She asks Joab why he would swallow up the inheritance of the LORD, and her city gives up Sheba (20:16-22).

2 Samuel 21.summary: There is a famine in David's days three years, and David enquires of the LORD, who says It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites (2 Samuel 21:1–2). The Gibeonites say they want no silver or gold, but seven of Saul's sons to hang up before the LORD in Gibeah, and David says I will give them (2 Samuel 21:3–6). The king spares Mephibosheth because of the LORD's oath between David and Jonathan, and gives up two sons of Rizpah and five of Michal's, who are hanged in the hill before the LORD in the days of barley harvest (2 Samuel 21:7–9). Rizpah spreads sackcloth on the rock and suffers neither the birds of the air by day nor the beasts of the field by night to touch the bodies (2 Samuel 21:10). David takes the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabeshgilead and buries them with the hanged men's bones in the sepulchre of Kish, and after that God is intreated for the land (2 Samuel 21:11–14). Four Philistine giants are slain by David's men, and David's men swear he shall go no more out to battle, that he quench not the light of Israel (2 Samuel 21:15–22).
2 Samuel 21.whereWeAre: Chapter 20 ended with Sheba's revolt put down. Chapters 21 to 24 are a closing section that steps back from the main story. Chapter 21 tells of a famine, the Gibeonites' claim for justice, Rizpah's watch, and wars with Philistine giants (21:1-22). Chapter 22 gives David's song.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Asks the LORD about the famine, gives up seven of Saul's sons, and buries the bones (21:1-14).

keyFigures.name: The Gibeonites
keyFigures.role: Ask for seven men of Saul's house because he slew them (21:2-9).

keyFigures.name: Rizpah
keyFigures.role: Keeps the birds and beasts from the bodies from the beginning of harvest until rain (21:8-10).

keyFigures.name: Mephibosheth son of Jonathan
keyFigures.role: Spared because of the oath between David and Jonathan (21:7).

keyFigures.name: The men of Jabeshgilead
keyFigures.role: Had the bones of Saul and Jonathan, which David takes and buries (21:12-14).

keyFigures.name: Abishai and David's men
keyFigures.role: Slay the Philistine giants and tell David not to go out to battle again (21:16-22).

keyThemes.theme: A wrong that was not forgotten
keyThemes.explanation: The famine is for Saul's bloody house because he slew the Gibeonites (21:1-9).
David spares Mephibosheth because of the LORD's oath between him and Jonathan (21:7).
Her long vigil leads David to bury the bones properly (21:10-14).

2 Samuel 22.summary: David speaks the words of this song to the LORD in the day that the LORD had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul (2 Samuel 22:1). He says The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer, my shield, and the horn of my salvation (2 Samuel 22:2–4). He tells how the waves of death compassed him, he called on the LORD, and the earth shook, smoke went up, and the LORD rode upon a cherub and delivered him out of many waters (2 Samuel 22:5–20). The LORD rewarded him according to his righteousness, for with the merciful he will shew himself merciful (2 Samuel 22:21–28). Thou art my lamp, O LORD, and by my God have I leaped over a wall, as for God, his way is perfect (2 Samuel 22:29–31). God is his strength and makes his feet like hinds' feet and teaches his hands to war (2 Samuel 22:32–43). He praises the LORD among the heathen and says the LORD sheweth mercy to his anointed, unto David, and to his seed for evermore (2 Samuel 22:44–51).
2 Samuel 22.whereWeAre: Chapter 21 ended with David's men keeping him from battle. Chapter 22 is a long song of thanks to the LORD for rescuing David from his enemies, and it appears again as Psalm 18 (22:1-51). Chapter 23 gives David's last words.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Sings that the LORD is his rock, fortress, and deliverer (22:1-4,47-51).

keyFigures.name: The LORD
keyFigures.role: Hears David's cry, comes down in storm, delivers him, and shews mercy to his anointed (22:7-20,51).

keyFigures.name: David's enemies, including Saul
keyFigures.role: The ones from whom the LORD delivered him (22:1,18,38-41).

keyThemes.explanation: David calls the LORD his rock, fortress, shield, and high tower (22:2-4).
David says the LORD delivered him because he delighted in him (22:17-20,47-50).
As for God, his way is perfect, and the word of the LORD is tried (22:26-37).

2 Samuel 23.summary: These are the last words of David, the sweet psalmist of Israel, who says The Spirit of the LORD spake by me, and his word was in my tongue (2 Samuel 23:1–2). He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God, and he shall be as the light of the morning, and God hath made with him an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure (2 Samuel 23:3–5). The sons of Belial shall be thrust away as thorns (2 Samuel 23:6–7). The chapter lists David's mighty men, Adino the Eznite, who lifted up his spear against eight hundred, Eleazar, whose hand clave unto the sword, and Shammah, who defended a piece of ground full of lentiles (2 Samuel 23:8–12). Three mighty men break through the host of the Philistines to draw water from the well of Bethlehem, but David will not drink it, and pours it out unto the LORD, saying is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives (2 Samuel 23:13–17). The list goes on with Abishai and Benaiah, and ends with Uriah the Hittite, thirty and seven in all (2 Samuel 23:18–39).
2 Samuel 23.whereWeAre: Chapter 22 was David's song of thanks. Chapter 23 gives his last words about a just ruler and God's covenant, then a list of his bravest men, ending with the name of Uriah the Hittite (23:1-39). Chapter 24 closes the book with the census.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Speaks his last words and pours out the water as an offering (23:1-7,15-17).

keyFigures.name: Adino, Eleazar, and Shammah
keyFigures.role: The three mighty men, who each stood alone against the Philistines (23:8-12).

keyFigures.name: The three who drew the water
keyFigures.role: Break through the Philistine host to bring water from Bethlehem (23:13-16).

keyFigures.name: Abishai
keyFigures.role: Chief of the three, who lifted up his spear against three hundred (23:18-19).

keyFigures.name: Benaiah
keyFigures.role: Slays two lionlike men of Moab, a lion in a pit, and an Egyptian (23:20-23).

keyFigures.name: Uriah the Hittite
keyFigures.role: The last name on the list of thirty and seven (23:39).

keyThemes.explanation: He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God (23:3-4).
David says God hath made with him an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure (23:5).
David will not drink water bought with the blood of his men, and pours it out to the LORD (23:15-17).

2 Samuel 24.summary: The anger of the LORD is kindled against Israel, and David is moved to say Go, number Israel and Judah, and Joab says why doth my lord the king delight in this thing, but the king's word prevails (2 Samuel 24:1–4). Joab and the captains go through the land, and after nine months and twenty days they bring in eight hundred thousand men in Israel and five hundred thousand in Judah (2 Samuel 24:5–9). David's heart smites him, and he says I have sinned greatly in that I have done, and Gad the prophet offers him seven years of famine, three months of flight, or three days of pestilence (2 Samuel 24:10–13). David says let us fall now into the hand of the LORD, for his mercies are great, and seventy thousand men die, and when the angel stretches out his hand upon Jerusalem, the LORD says It is enough, stay now thine hand (2 Samuel 24:14–16). David says Lo, I have sinned, but these sheep, what have they done (2 Samuel 24:17). Gad tells David to rear an altar in the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite, and David buys it for fifty shekels of silver, saying neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing, and the plague is stayed (2 Samuel 24:18–25).
2 Samuel 24.whereWeAre: Chapter 23 ended with David's mighty men. Chapter 24 closes the book: David numbers the people, a plague falls, and David buys Araunah's threshingfloor and builds an altar, where the plague stops (24:1-25). 1 Kings follows, with David's last days and Solomon.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.role: Numbers the people, confesses his sin, chooses the LORD's hand, and buys the threshingfloor (24:1-2,10,14,17-25).

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.role: Asks the king not to do it, then does the counting (24:3-9).

keyFigures.name: Gad the prophet
keyFigures.role: Gives David the three choices and tells him to build an altar (24:11-14,18-19).

keyFigures.name: Araunah the Jebusite
keyFigures.role: Offers the threshingfloor free, but David pays (24:18-24).

keyFigures.name: The angel
keyFigures.role: Stretches out his hand on Jerusalem, and the LORD says It is enough (24:15-16).

keyThemes.explanation: David is moved to number Israel and Judah, and his heart smites him afterward (24:1-10).
David chooses the hand of the LORD, whose mercies are great, and the LORD says It is enough (24:13-16).
David will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD of that which doth cost him nothing (24:18-25).

explainedReferences.explanation: Same event: David's census, the plague, and purchase of the threshing floor; they differ on who incited the census.
